text:
Colorado scored eight times on a night when the numbers say it should have scored about three. The Avalanche generated 3.36 expected goals to Los Angeles's 2.9, enough for a 58 percent claim on deserving the win, but nowhere near an 8-4 margin. The gap came from power-play finishing: Colorado cashed four of five chances, including Artturi Lehkonen's pair at 18:34 of the second and 15:06 of the third, the second of which carried a 24 percent chance of scoring and made it 8-4.

Los Angeles actually controlled the opening period, out-chancing Colorado 1.48 to 0.73 in expected goals, and kept pace with 62 shot attempts to 50 overall. Brian Dumoulin tied it at 1-1 on a 2 percent look, but Parker Kelly answered at 17:58 and Nathan MacKinnon made it 3-1 just 23 seconds into the second on the power play. The Kings kept coming, with shorthanded goals from Joel Armia and Trevor Moore pulling them within a goal twice, yet each time Colorado had the next answer. MacKinnon scored again at 8:33 on a 4 percent chance, and Nicolas Roy's poke at 16:01 made it 5-2.

The real separator was goaltending and the penalty kill. Darcy Kuemper allowed 8 goals on 3.36 expected, 4.64 goals worse than an average goalie would have, while Mackenzie Blackwood, at 1.1 below expected, gave up 4 on 2.9. Los Angeles took four more minors than it drew in the power-play column, going 0 for 4 itself against Colorado's four conversions. MacKinnon finished with two goals on eight shots, Brock Nelson added a goal and two assists, and Colorado took the win despite not being the clearly better team for long stretches.
